newsitem.title: USA: Frontier sees Q1 net loss after $0.32 charge.
newsitem.headline: Frontier sees Q1 net loss after $0.32 charge.

text.p: Frontier Corp said Thursday it expected lower than anticipated revenue growth and higher bad debt expense in its long distance operations to result in a net loss after charges in the first quarter.

The company said it expected to report a net loss in the range of $0.07 to $0.10 per share in the first quarter after taking account of two non-recurring charges that, when combined, would slash reported earnings per share by $0.32.
Frontier said first quarter operating earnings, excluding charges, would be in the range of $0.22 to $0.25 per share. The First Call consensus called for $0.30 per share.
The first quarter earnings warning follows a similar disappointing surprise in the fourth quarter of 1996.

For the fourth quarter the company reported operating earnings of $0.30 per share, $0.02 below the consensus estimate according to Zacks. Net earnings were $0.06 per share versus $0.34 per share in the 1995 fourth quarter.
In a statement issued Thursday, Frontier company said it expected revenue in its core long distance business to be in the range of $400 million.
Frontier expects to report actual first quarter results on April 23.
First quarter long distance business revenues in the range of $400 million would be roughly flat sequentially compared with the fourth quarter of 1996, the company said.
The $0.32 in first quarter charges result from a $0.38 per share charge partially offset by an $0.06 per share gain.

It said it will record a non-recurring charge of $96.6 million, or $0.38 per share, principally related to the writeoff of certain network costs no longer necessary to support long distance traffic volumes in certain areas.
The $0.06 gain is tied to sale of its 69.5 percent stake in the South Alabama Cellular Communications Partnership.
Frontier sold the partnership stake to Alltel Corp.

The company said it is experiencing slower than anticipated revenue growth from recent initiatives which include targeting larger business accounts and pursuing opportunities in the prepaid calling card market.
It said net revenue will include the impact of over $5 million of incremental bad debt associated with two of the company's customers.
The migration of 1+ traffic from Frontier's largest wholesale customer previously announced for the fourth quarter has continued into the first quarter, the company said.

Recognizing the change in traffic volumes, the company took an inventory of its existing long distance network and facilities and identified those no longer necessary to support Frontier's revenue and traffic volumes, it said.
This was behind the previously mentioned charge of $0.38 a share planned for the first quarter.

Frontier said paring back facilities in its leased network will not impede revenue growth, but will assist in the migration of a majority of Frontier's traffic onto a fiber optic network it is building with Qwest Communications Corp.

"We've begun to execute a plan that we believe will provide Frontier with the most robust and cost-efficient network in the industry by the end of 1998," said Louis Massaro, Frontier's chief financial officer.
-- Eric Auchard, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1736
